channel.title: The Melbourne Indian
channel.description: Independent, free-to-read news for Melbourne's Indian communities in English, Hindi and Punjabi.

item.title: Westpac is lending to 30 per cent fewer housing construction projects, bank boss tells MPs
item.description: The heads of Westpac and ANZ faced a parliamentary inquiry on Thursday. Commonwealth Bank and NAB are due to give evidence today.

item.title: Free Diwali celebration at Queen Victoria Market this Saturday
item.description: Dance, music and dozens of food stalls in C Shed on 14 November, from 9am to 4pm. No booking needed.

item.title: India renames its tourist visa a 'visitor visa' and cuts visa types from 13 to nine
item.description: The new system is due to start by the end of the year. It matters if non-Indian family or friends are planning a trip to India with you.

item.title: Three Tamil Nadu temple treasures handed back to India in Canberra
item.description: A Bhadrakali trident, a Nandi and a six-headed Karthikeya were formally returned this week, fulfilling a promise made at the Modi–Albanese summit in Melbourne in July.

item.title: Leakes Road in Tarneit to be widened to four lanes, with work due to start early next year
item.description: Wyndham City Council has awarded the construction contract for the $25.5 million duplication between Tarneit Road and Derrimut Road.

item.title: Pancreatic cancer campaigner Cherie Dear named Victoria's Australian of the Year
item.description: An autism researcher, a young health charity founder and a Horsham mechanic who gives cars to young people were also recognised. All four now go to the national awards in January.

item.title: Cummins calls Khawaja's ball-tampering claims 'complete and utter nonsense'
item.description: Australia's Test captain says he did not know sandpaper was being used in Cape Town in 2018, and that his former teammate is being 'casual' with people's reputations.

item.title: Federal government considers softening its cuts to backpacker visas after farm and tourism outcry
item.description: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke says the overall migration numbers are not up for negotiation, but he is talking to industry about 'a better way' to reach them.

item.title: VCE students warned not to buy 'leaked' exams after hack, as police cybercrime squad investigates
item.description: The exam authority says offers of leaked papers are fake and designed to exploit anxious students. Its website is still offline, cutting access to study materials.

item.title: Workers at Malmsbury youth justice centre paid almost $7 million in compensation for violence, as the reopened centre scales up
item.description: Department of Justice figures released under freedom of information show a violent incident was logged every 2.6 days on average before the centre closed in 2023.

item.title: Bupa aged care residents asked to pay about $42 a day for a package that includes hot breakfasts
item.description: Residents who don't sign up get a continental breakfast. Bupa says dietitian-recommended cooked protein is available to everyone.

item.title: Greens set sights on Labor's inner-north heartland, with Northcote the closest fight
item.description: The Greens are targeting Northcote, Preston, Pascoe Vale and Footscray at the 28 November election. In Northcote, 184 votes decided the seat last time.

item.title: 1,037 candidates will be on Victorian ballot papers, and the order has now been drawn
item.description: Nominations have closed for the 28 November state election, so you can now look up exactly who is standing where you live.

item.title: Microsoft outage knocks out Outlook and Teams worldwide; services starting to recover
item.description: Email, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services went down early on Friday, Melbourne time. Microsoft says a fix is bringing servers back, but has not said what caused it.

item.title: Missing teenager William found alive in Gippsland bush after six days
item.description: A police helicopter crew spotted the 17-year-old asleep in a dry riverbed near Walhalla East. He is sunburnt, cut and exhausted, but talking and smiling, police say.

item.title: Disability advocates lose federal funding, and a regional Victorian legal service stops taking new clients
item.description: Villamanta Disability Rights Legal Service is losing almost a third of its funding as Canberra replaces a decades-old advocacy program. The Department says the new model follows the disability royal commission.

item.title: This weekend: Malabar food and music, Diwali at the market, and a free interfaith festival
item.description: A taste of northern Kerala in Abbotsford tonight, free Diwali celebrations at Queen Victoria Market on Saturday, and faith communities coming together in St Kilda on Sunday.

item.title: Parks Victoria stops campsite bookings after booking provider breach, warns of WhatsApp scams
item.description: Existing bookings still stand, but no new bookings or changes can be made for now. Parks Victoria says it never contacts customers on WhatsApp.

item.title: NAB to repay $169 million to 66,000 staff it underpaid over 14 years, and pays a record $2 million 'contrition payment'
item.description: The bank reported the problems itself in 2019. Some workers are owed under $5; others more than $87,000. The average is about $1,900.

item.title: VCAA website hacked mid-exams, but authority says no sign VCE papers were accessed
item.description: A hacker posted claims on the exam authority's home page that VCE papers had been sold to students. The VCAA says exams will go ahead as normal and has called in police.

item.title: Labor promises Clare's Law and a dating-app ban for violent offenders if re-elected
item.description: Victorians could ask police whether a partner has a history of family violence under a scheme both major parties now say they will bring in.

item.title: AI companies could face criminal charges in Australia after an AI agent breached a Medicare website
item.description: The federal government says it has accepted every recommendation of a review into the OpenAI incident, and is considering what it calls a world-first offence for AI companies.

item.title: Macquarie Bank faces $14 million penalty over its savings 'Welcome Rate', as ASIC tells savers to check their interest
item.description: Nearly 40,000 customers have already been paid $8.8 million. The regulator says anyone on a bonus or introductory rate should check they are getting what they were promised.

item.title: New home loans suffer their biggest quarterly fall on record, led by investors pulling back
item.description: Investor lending dropped by almost a third in the September quarter. First home buyer loans fell too, but buyers still made up more than a third of owner-occupier loans.

item.title: Severe alcohol-related liver disease is hitting younger Victorians and more women, report finds
item.description: A Burnet Institute report for the Foundation for Alcohol Research and Education found about four in ten hospital admissions for alcohol-associated hepatitis were people under their mid-40s.

item.title: ASIC sues Commonwealth Bank, alleging it overcharged 42,000 business customers $8.5 million in hidden fees
item.description: The corporate regulator says CBA's CommBiz terms did not disclose a second fee on direct debits and credits. The bank says it found the problem itself and has already repaid more than $26 million.

item.title: Abhishek Awasthi elected Mayor of Greater Bendigo
item.description: The Kennington Ward councillor, who came to Australia from Himachal Pradesh to study, will lead the regional city for the next year. The Indian Sun reports he is its first mayor of Indian origin.

item.title: Home loan repayments go up from Friday as all four big banks pass on the Reserve Bank's rate rise
item.description: CBA, NAB, ANZ and Westpac are lifting variable home loan rates by 0.25 percentage points from 13 November, after the Reserve Bank raised the cash rate to 4.85 per cent.

item.title: Labor promises $420 million for more V/Line trains, with Melton and Wyndham Vale getting the biggest boost
item.description: Premier Ben Carroll says more than 550 extra regional trips a week would be added if Labor is re-elected on 28 November. Labor also used a budget office analysis to attack the Liberals' surplus plan.

item.title: Pay rises on $45,000 a year will be hit hardest by 'bracket creep', research finds
item.description: Without tax cuts, people on about $45,000 and those near the top tax bracket would lose more than half of their real pay growth to tax over a decade, the e61 Institute says.
